purpose: Complete six-stanza Watts hymn on Christ's resurrection and ascension with explicitly editorial ST. ANNE pairing.
reviewNotes: Checked Book II hymn 76 wording against the stored 1818-printing transcription, not page scans.
Optional-stanza brackets and stanza numbers are editorial apparatus and were removed; wording and punctuation were retained.
Common Meter editorial pairing uses existing checksum-verified MIDI and RDF evidence. Synthesized playback, not a performance recording.
Poetic language must not be presented as direct KJV Scripture.

entries.title: Hosanna to the Prince of Light
stanzas:
Hosanna to the Prince of Light,
That cloth'd himself in clay,
Enter'd the iron gates of death,
And tore the bars away.

Death is no more the king of dread
Since our Immanuel rose,
He took the tyrant's sting away,
And spoil'd our hellish foes.

See how the Conqueror mounts aloft,
And to his Father flies,
With scars of honour in his flesh,
And triumph in his eyes.

There our exalted Saviour reigns,
And scatters blessings down,
Our Jesus fills the middle seat
Of the celestial throne.

Raise your devotion, mortal tongues,
To reach his bless'd abode,
Sweet be the accents of your songs
To our incarnate God.

Bright angels, strike your loudest strings,
Your sweetest voices raise,
Let heaven, and all created things,
Sound our Immanuel's praise.
